title: Signed Windows Utility Referencing A Script Protocol Handler
detection_hypothesis: If a signed script-capable utility is used as an execution proxy, the command line will contain an inline script protocol prefix instead of a file path.

field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.
field_semantics.CommandLine: Full command line including arguments as supplied to the process.

collection_prerequisites: A process creation source is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 1 or Security Event ID 4688).
Command-line auditing is enabled when Security 4688 is the only available source.
expected_collection_gaps: Security 4688 without command-line auditing provides no CommandLine value.
Short-lived processes may be lost if the agent is restarted during collection.
normalization_assumptions: Image and ParentImage are absolute paths using backslash separators.
CommandLine retains the original argument order and spacing.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines lowercase paths; the lab matcher is case-insensitive by default.
Sysmon and 4688 differ in parent process fidelity and in User field formatting.
retention_considerations: Process creation is high volume; 30 to 90 days of hot retention is typical.
expected_volume: Very low on modern estates; occasional on hosts running legacy tooling.
false_positive_strategy: Legacy internal applications are the dominant benign source. Identify them by the invoking parent process and by the stable script text, then exclude that exact combination instead of the whole utility.
tuning_guidance: Scope exclusions with both ParentImage and a distinctive command-line substring. Excluding mshta.exe outright removes coverage for the entire proxy execution technique.
test_strategy: Positive cases cover the javascript and vbscript protocol prefixes. Negative cases cover a local HTML application file, a different utility using the same protocol text, and an unrelated system binary.
unmapped_defensive_objects_reason: No Detection Strategy, Analytic, or Data Component identifier for this technique was present in the pinned ATT&CK extraction used by this lab. Defensive arrays are left empty rather than populated with unverified identifiers. Unmapped techniques: T1218.005.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
